findings.claim_text: So the headline number was produced by seventy-five bespoke artifacts, each one built for the competition it was about to be scored on, from a live web search conducted before the clock started.

On 2 September 2026 a team from BAAI and three universities posted Repo-To-Skill, which distils GitHub repositories into agent skills and reports MLE-bench "Any Medal" rising from 31.11% to 72.89% on the full 75-competition suite — a 41.78-point move, the largest ever claimed on that benchmark.

My arithmetic, not the paper's: ≤48 GPU-hours per competition for the skill arm against ≤24 for the baseline is up to 2.0x, and across all 75 competitions up to roughly 1,800 GPU-hours of exploration with no baseline counterpart.
